1947, May 10
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O.F.M. Cap.
SAINT FELIX FRIARY HUNTINGTON, INDIANA
May 10, 1947
Mr. C. W. Seery 18 W. Lawrence St. Pontiac, Michigan
My Dear Mr. Seery:
God bless you and your friends, and us all. I hope you are well and that your friend-patient is not losing. We received your wire some nights ago and enrolled M. O'Laugh'n in the Seraphic Mass Association as an emergency case. Today we received your special and are enrolling as the enclosed will indicate, a perpetual member.
Thanks be to the merciful God, we have had several notable cases of cures reported as through this means here as, especially in Detroit, and esewhere.
Rather than detail instructions what for anyone to follow, I am going to give you here a brief resume of a letter I wrote several months back to a presbiterian whose father, grand-father and great- grandfather were all presbiterian ministers and who I believe is now taking instructions or is possibly already a practical Catholic. In fact there are two cases here involved, - bothe noncatholic, therefore, Seery or an 0' would say: "on the other side of the fence". It follows about thus :
" ... I am sure dear Mr. R.J., I tolde you of the W. case, noted here just about two months ahead of yous. Lest I be mistaken, However, here it is in brief. 'March 26, 1943. Mrs. W. ... W. was a methodist, had been given up after the third operation on a brain- cancer as destined for death inside six months. (The first opera- tion was on February 23rd). Mrs. Wh. weeping was introduced same
